name: Поля, пастки й відкритий напад
description:
In this lesson we focus on the discovered attack. As in the previous lessons on pitfalls, there seem to be two good moves in each position, but as you know by now, only one move wins material. The checkmating square plays an important role again!

With a discovered attack we can attack two pieces, a piece and the king or a piece and a mating square.

Example 1 is all about cleverly attacking a piece and a checkmate square.

In Example 2, you can attack two pieces at the same time, but be careful! In this case, the defender can escape with a counterattack on a mating square if you choose the wrong continuation!

What do you have to do?
Win material by performing a discovered attack. Be careful not to give the other player a chance to defend by counterattacking.

examples.text:
1.Bc6! attacks both the rook and the mating square e8. White wins material: 1...Ra8 2.Bxa8.

Also 1.Bc2 (red arrow) looks strong, but does not yield any material. In this case Black can remove the rook and at the same time cover the mating square e8 with 1...Ra8! (green arrow). The difference with 1.Bc6 is that square a8 is now not safe.

1.Ne6! attacks both the rook and the knight. Black can try to attack square c1 with 1...Rc5, but after 2.Nxc5 White has won material.

1.Nf3 (red arrow) also attacks the rook and knight, however 1...Rc5 (green arrow) comes to the rescue. After 2.Rxd7 Rc1+ white can interpose the rook and then the knight, but afterwards would be mated! Making luft is better than 2.Rxd7, but then black has all the time in the world to move the knight to safety.

texts: Loose pieces drop off the board.
